verses.1: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.2: May every grave in the land of Israel be sanctified for me. May every womb in the land of Israel belong to me, both in humans and animals. This is what I desire.
verses.3: And Moses said to the people, “Remember this day when you left Egypt as slaves. In God’s strength, He brought you out of there. No fire will ever be able to destroy you.”
verses.4: Today, you will go out in the month of Aviv.
verses.5: And it shall be that the LORD will bring you into the land of Canaan, the land of Israel, Judah, Ephron, Hivviyah, and Yevus. This land will be a place where you can eat milk and honey. You will serve this Lord during this month.
verses.6: For seven days, he shall eat matzot. On the seventh day, it is a holiday for Yahweh.
verses.7: It will be eaten on the seven days; it will not be seen by you as meat, nor will it be seen in all your lands.
verses.8: And you told your son on that day, saying, “In this regard, Jehovah has done this for me when I left Egypt.”
verses.9: And it shall be a reminder to you, so that you may remember it constantly. This will make the laws of Jehovah known to you, for in your hands is the power with which Jehovah has freed you from Egypt.
verses.10: And you have kept this law forever, from ancient times to the present.
verses.11: And it shall be, when Jehovah comes into the land of Canaan, as it was promised to you and to your ancestors, and it shall be given to you.
verses.12: And you shall carry all those who are under heaven as offerings to the LORD. And all those who live in animals, they will be a reminder of the LORD for you.
verses.13: And every hair of the woolly sheep will be plucked out. And if it isn’t plucked out, then it will be destroyed. And everything related to human beings will also be plucked out from your bodies.
verses.14: And it shall be like this: Your son will ask you tomorrow, “What is this?” And you will say to him, with firm voice, “The LORD has brought us out of Egypt, from the house of slavery.”
verses.15: And it became difficult for Pharaoh to send us away. Thus, Jehovah killed every animal that was killed in the land of Egypt, from human beings to animals. Therefore, I offer sacrifices to Jehovah for all those who suffered. All the animals that were killed by me are now forgiven.
verses.16: And it shall be a sign for you, and a reminder to you that through the strength of your hands, Jehovah will bring us out of Egypt.
verses.17: And when Pharaoh sent out the people, he did not honor God along the way through the land of Egypt. For God said that He would not bless the people if they continued to fight in battle and returned from Egypt.
verses.18: And God led the people across the Sea of Galilee. Seventy thousand men of Israel went up from the land of Egypt.
verses.19: And Moses took Joshua with him, because the Lord had commanded to take away the sin of the Israelites. He said, “May God punish you, and may he take away my own life from among you.”
verses.20: And they traveled from the ships, and they stopped at those places on the edge of the desert.
verses.21: And Jehovah went before them by day, with a cloud as a guide for their path; and by night, with a fire to illuminate their way, so that they could walk both by day and by night.
verses.22: The pillar of the sky will not be removed during the day, and the pillar of fire will not be removed at night, before the people.
